what_its_for: Relugolix is used to treat advanced prostate cancer in men by lowering the amount of testosterone in your body, which helps slow the growth of cancer cells. It is also used in combination with other medicines to treat heavy menstrual bleeding caused by uterine fibroids in women, and to treat painful periods caused by endometriosis.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. If you are taking it for prostate cancer (Orgovyx), you will take it alone. If you are taking it for fibroids or endometriosis (Myfembree), it comes as a combination pill with other medicines.
dosing: For prostate cancer (Orgovyx): The usual starting dose on Day 1 is 360 mg (3 tablets of 120 mg), then 120 mg (1 tablet) once daily after that. For uterine fibroids or endometriosis (Myfembree): Take 1 tablet once daily. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may be different based on your condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. If you stop taking relugolix for more than 7 days in a row, contact your doctor before restarting, as you may need a higher starting dose again.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container. Keep the container tightly closed and away from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium at the same time as relugolix — wait at least 2 hours before or after taking these products. Avoid taking certain seizure medicines, antibiotics, or antifungal medicines without telling your doctor first, as they may affect how well relugolix works. Do not take any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath (signs of heart problems); sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness, or difficulty speaking (signs of a possible stroke or blood clot); bone pain or signs of bone thinning such as a fracture from a minor injury; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; depression, mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm; hot flashes that are severe or interfering with daily life; unusual weight gain; or if you are a woman and you think you might be pregnant.
when_it_works: For prostate cancer, your testosterone levels should drop significantly within about 4 weeks of starting treatment. For uterine fibroids or endometriosis, you may start to notice a reduction in pain or bleeding within the first 1 to 3 months of treatment. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Relugolix can cause serious harm to an unborn baby and must NOT be used during pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant must use effective non-hormonal birth control during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Older adults: Older patients, especially men with prostate cancer, may have a higher risk of heart problems, bone thinning, and falls. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose or monitoring may need to be adjusted.
